source_window.data_date: Official HM Land Registry technical specification accessed 2026-10-06
source_window.license: The technical-specification page is publicly readable; access to the National Polygon Dataset itself requires an HM Land Registry account, a signed licence and payment.

field_evidence.dataset_scope: HM Land Registry states that the National Polygon Dataset is the published dataset of HMLR Index Polygons for England and Wales and is a subset of the Land Register containing registered titles relating to land or property.
field_evidence.title_polygon_relationship: The technical specification states that title plan and register share the title number; every registered title has at least one index polygon; each index polygon has a unique Poly_ID; and the registered-title to polygon relationship is managed through the title number.
field_evidence.mandatory_geometry_identifier_fields: The National Polygon table requires Shape (Geometry), Poly_ID (unique polygon reference) and Title_No (unique registered-title identifier), with Shape defined as a single-area geometry.
field_evidence.extent_limit: The specification states that an index polygon represents title extent but can be the same size, larger or smaller than the title-plan extent and should not be relied on to show the exact extent of registered titles.
field_evidence.access_limit: The technical specification is publicly readable without login, but access to the National Polygon Dataset itself requires creating an account, agreeing a licence and paying for the dataset.
field_evidence.target_limit: This public technical-specification window contains no Forge Cottage / TN25 7JX target record, Title_No, Poly_ID, Shape geometry or canonical bbox.
field_evidence.parcel_promotion_rule: No canonical parcel ID, geometry or bbox is promoted from specification metadata. Target-specific title/polygon binding and all spatial join/materialization remain local OpenCode work.

first_missing_criterion: Verified BUILDING_PRESENT canonical parcel geometry/bbox for this producer. HM Land Registry's unused public National Polygon Dataset technical specification defines the target-capable mandatory fields Shape, Poly_ID and Title_No and explains the title-number relationship to index polygons, but the full National Polygon Dataset requires an account, signed licence and payment and this public/no-login specification window contains no Forge Cottage target record. The specification also states that index polygons are indicative and may be larger or smaller than the title-plan extent, so they are not exact registered-title boundaries. Local OpenCode or authorised HM Land Registry access must bind the exact target title/polygon and canonical bbox; after that, bind one unused exact official DEM/LIDAR tile or metadata-index record to that bbox.
exact_blocker: The method was materially changed from the VOA Council Tax public postcode/address search to HM Land Registry's National Polygon Dataset technical specification and data-model/access channel. The official page is public/no-login and identifies the precise machine-readable fields needed for target binding, but the target dataset itself is account/licence/payment gated and no Forge Cottage Title_No, Poly_ID or Shape is exposed in this window. In addition, HMLR states that an index polygon should not be relied on as the exact registered-title extent. No canonical parcel ID, geometry or bbox is asserted; spatial join/materialization remains local OpenCode work.
